title: Variable Scope, Attributes, and Name Reference Pollution
platform_conditions: bash 4.3+ for declare -n namerefs; printf -v, declare, and export -f are bash/ksh features not present in POSIX sh; readonly assumptions differ across bash versions
security_mechanism: Inside a function, an assignment to an undeclared name writes the global scope, so two concurrent invocations of a helper that sets 'status' or 'user' without local overwrite each other's security-relevant state. Worse, several builtins take the variable NAME as data: declare -n ref="$user_input" makes ref an alias to whatever variable the external input names (including readonly or PATH), and declare "$name=$value", printf -v "$name", and read "$name" perform an assignment whose left side is attacker-chosen. export and export -f carry selected names and even function bodies into every child process, so a helper's internal state or a whole function implementation escapes the process boundary; and code that treats a readonly declaration as tamper-proof can be surprised, since unset/duplicate handling of readonly names differs across shell versions.

source_sink_clues.source: Externally supplied identifier strings (config keys, query or flag names turned into variable names, environment-derived key names in CI) and shared-variable names in scripts run concurrently or re-entrant.
source_sink_clues.sink: declare -n / local -n with input-derived names; declare "$name=$value"; printf -v "$name"; read into input-derived names; assignments to non-local names inside functions on security paths; export/export -f of secret-bearing or security-relevant names

tracking_guards: Check every function-local assignment is declared local; check any builtin taking a variable name validates it against ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ and an allowlist before use; check secrets are passed via files or fd inheritance rather than export; check no export -f is used near privilege boundaries.
not_candidate_when: The name argument is validated against a strict identifier pattern and an allowlist before reaching declare/printf -v/read, all function variables are local and the script is single-threaded so no cross-call state persists, or nothing sensitive is exported and the child processes are trusted.
public_references: CWE-74: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/74.html
Bash Reference Manual: Shell Parameter Expansion (nameref declarations) — https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Shell-Parameter-Expansion.html
